newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle sell $63-$63.25,thin - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle sell $63-$63.25,thin - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales Wednesday were slow at $63.00 to $63.25 per cwt, steady to up $0.25 from Tuesday's brisk trade, feedlot sources said.

About 11,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area at mostly $63.00, with a few at $63.25, they said. Weekly movement was pegged near 81,500 head. The Panhandle showlist was pegged near 80,500 head.

An estimated 1,000 head sold in Kansas at $63.00, which brought the week to date figure near 77,000, the sources said. The showlist in Kansas was estimated near 89,000 head earlier in the week, they said.
Big supplies of market-ready fed cattle has kept prices near $63.00 this week, which was down $6.00 from last month's top price of $69.00, USDA statistics showed.
Fed cattle prices have eroded quickly since then as supplies expanded and demand slipped when retailers completed buying beef for Memorial Day promotions, market sources said.

Continued expansion of market-ready cattle since early to mid-May not only pushed fed cattle prices lower, but drove beef values down as packers discounted offerings to maintain beef inventories at manageable levels, they said. Beef prices were down again Wednesday, but movement remained strong.
Beef prices were quoted down $0.65 to $1.10 per cwt, with 479 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA reported. Heavyweight choice was at $98.53, down $1.10 from Tuesday, but down $3.75 from a week ago.
Fabricated beef movement for the week to date was 1,020 loads, up 1.6 percent from the same period a week ago at 880, USDA statistics showed.
